title: Nuclear Fission and Fusion
notes: Fission splits a heavy nucleus into medium-mass fragments, often after neutron absorption. Fusion combines light nuclei. Either can release energy when products have greater total binding energy than reactants.
Reaction energy follows mass-energy conservation: Q=(mi−mf)c². Positive Q means the final rest mass is lower and the difference appears as kinetic energy, radiation or excitation.

Uranium-235 fission can release several neutrons. A sustained chain reaction requires, on average, enough neutrons to induce further fissions; a reactor controls this multiplication with neutron absorbers and moderators.

Deuterium–tritium fusion can form helium-4 and a neutron, releasing about 17.6 MeV. The positively charged nuclei must approach closely despite Coulomb repulsion, requiring high temperature and adequate confinement.
Fission is used in nuclear power stations; fusion powers stars. Practical fusion requires maintaining a hot dense plasma long enough for reaction energy to exceed losses.

specificConditions: **Fission vs Fusion Energy Release:** Both release energy by moving toward higher $BE/A$ (iron peak). Fission splits heavy nuclei ($A > 56$) into medium fragments. Fusion combines light nuclei ($A < 56$) into heavier ones. Both increase the average $BE/A$ of the system.

**Chain Reaction Requirement:** Fission of $^{235}$U by thermal neutrons produces ~2.4 fast neutrons/fission. A sustained chain reaction requires at least 1 neutron to cause another fission ($k \ge 1$). Critical mass is the minimum mass where neutron losses are balanced by productions. Moderators (graphite, water) slow neutrons to thermal energies to increase capture probability.

**Fusion Conditions:** Requires extreme temperature ($T \sim 10^7-10^8$ K) for nuclei to overcome Coulomb barrier ($kT \sim 1$ keV vs barrier $\sim 1$ MeV). Quantum tunneling allows fusion at lower energies. Plasma confinement (magnetic/inertial) is needed to maintain density and temperature long enough for significant fusion (Lawson criterion: $n\tau > 10^{20}$ m⁻³·s).
